items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the New York state urban development corporation act and the economic development law, in relation to establishing a certified service-disabled veteran-owned business enterprise development and lending program
items.lawCode: Add §16-c-1, UDC Act; amd §§210 & 211, Ec Dev L
items.lawSection: New York State Urban Development Corporation Act
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S5642

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the New York state urban development
corporation act and the economic development law, in relation to
establishing a certified service-disabled veteran-owned business
enterprise development and lending program

 PURPOSE :

To establish a certified service-disabled veteran-owned business
enterprise development and lending program, which will provide
financial and technical assistance to certified service-disabled
veteran-owned business enterprises.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :

Section one amends the New York state urban development corporation
act by adding a new section 16-c-1 to establish the certified
service-disabled veteran-owned business enterprise development and
lending program. This section establishes a revolving loan trust fund,
micro-loan program, a contracting program, direct financial
assistance, an incubator program, and a technical assistance program.
This section also requires the corporation to submit a biennial report
evaluating the effectiveness of the program.

Section two and three amends the economic development law by expanding
development centers to include certified service-disabled
veteran-owned business enterprises.

Section four is the effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

In May 2014, the Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Business Act (the
"Act") was signed into law and has since provided many
service-disabled veteran-owned businesses with state contracts.
However, in an effort to reach the Act's full participation goal,
further measures must be enacted to guarantee that certified
service-disabled veteran-owned business enterprises have the
opportunity for meaningful participation in the performance of state
contracts.

Any member of the armed forces must face the hardship of reintegrating
into society after serving his or her country. Unfortunately,
service-disabled veterans must bear this burden to a greater degree
because they are also coping with a disability incurred in the line of
duty. In an effort to assist veterans who have not only put their life
on the line to protect our country, but also incurred a disability
during that time, this bill will provide service-disabled veterans
with the necessary assistance for prosperity within their business
endeavors.

This bill would add a new section to the urban development
corporations act creating a business development and lending program
for certified service- disabled veteran-owned business enterprises,
providing these enterprises with access to financial and technical
assistance. The loans and services made available through this bill
will assist certified service-disabled veteran-owned business
enterprises in the purchasing of machinery or equipment and gain
acquisition or improvement of real property.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

New Bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect one year after it shall have become a law.
